title: bdi v1: a tree of work in flight
description:
`bdi` joins a beads tracker to a herdr session and draws one tree of work per
root, annotated with the live agent on each node. Read-only. This epic is the
whole of what `docs/design.md` calls v1.

**`docs/design.md` is a starting point, not gospel** — where it is ambiguous the
seat that hits the ambiguity decides with the code in front of it and records
what it chose, and `bdi-2bb.1` folds those in. Graeme's decision, 2026-08-30;
the fuller statement is below. `CLAUDE.md` carried the superseded "accepted
spec" line until `bdi-8df` took it out; that line had misrouted three seats in
a day, the last of which staged a finished P1 and refused to push.

**Effort slug: `v1`.** Every commy topic for this effort is built from it —
`#beady-eye/v1`, `#beady-eye/v1-decisions`, `#beady-eye/v1-<bead>`. A
replacement orchestrator must reuse this slug; inventing a fresh one posts into
topics no worker is subscribed to and registers a second `#general/fleet` line
for an effort that already has one.

**Delivery mode: direct, for this repo and it is the only repo.** Measured
2026-08-30: `gh api repos/CodeForBreakfast/beady-eye/rules/branches/main`
returns 403 *"Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public"*, and
`branches/main` reports `.protected: false`. Branch protection is not merely
unused here — it is unavailable on a private repo on the free plan. So workers
commit and push to `main`, beads close on push, and there is no PR cap and no
delivery ordering. That changes the day the repo goes public (bdi-iby), which
is exactly what bdi-fjo covers.

---

## Two halves, deliberately sequenced

1. **Core and `--json`** — `bdi-3um`, **done**, landed at `86cd807`. Config,
   both collectors, tree construction, the join, anomaly rules, failure
   classification, the snapshot and the CLI, up to and including the published
   JSON contract. 167 tests, clippy and fmt clean.
2. **The TUI** — `bdi-2bb`, the interface the name promises. Planned second and
   written against the real types, because a plan drafted against imagined ones
   is wrong the way the core's plan was: its task listing was wrong in all
   eleven tasks, and every seat that ran one found a real defect in its brief.

**v1 is done when** `bdi` with no flags draws the forest (`bdi-2bb.7`), it
works in a tracked repo with no config file (`bdi-wf5`), and CI runs the flake
checks on every push (`bdi-1a6`). All three are closed. **Release is not a v1
clause.** Graeme moved `bdi-7ph` under `bdi-iby` on 2026-08-31: a tag
publishing to crates.io and Nix needs a licence and a public repo, so it
belongs to going public. The TUI is built and runnable: `bdi-2bb.5`, `.6` and `.7` are
closed and there is no not-built exit path left in `main.rs` or `app.rs`, so a
seat that needs to see a real screen can render one. `bdi-vx7` closed on 2026-08-31 — it was worked, not deferred, and it is what
turned `bdi-7ao.13` and `.14` from design opinion into measurement.
`bdi-2bb.1` reconciles the design document after the rest lands.

**Explicitly not v1** (`docs/design.md`, *Non-goals for v1*): no writes to bd
beyond `herdr agent focus`, no Noctalia widget until the TUI has proved the
data model, no cross-machine view.

**Going public is not here.** That is `bdi-iby` — the licence, the scrub of
private infrastructure from tracked files, the Dolt host still in git history
(`bdi-a8s`), the PR gate, and **the release itself (`bdi-7ph`)**. Packaging into the NixOS config is tracked in that project as `nix-b8et4`.

---

## Roster

Everything below is in this project's tracker, and **no strand is worked by another project, so there are no tracking beads.**
One carries outbound coordination the orchestrator owns rather than work it
can staff: `bdi-7ph` points at `nix-b8et4` in the Summit-works project for the
consuming side of packaging. It goes through commy to that project's channel,
and it now lives under `bdi-iby`, not here.

**The TUI (`bdi-2bb`), seven children:**

**`.2` to `.9` are the original build and are closed.** This table is a reading
of the tracker, not the tracker: beads found mid-effort are added here as they
are filed, and `bd list --limit 0` is what a cold orchestrator should trust.

---

## Critical path

```
bdi-2bb.9 → .4 ─┐
bdi-2bb.3 → .5 ─┼→ .7 ─┐
         └→ .6 ─┘      ├→ bdi-2bb.1
bdi-wf5 → bdi-ijq → .6 │
bdi-2bb.2 ──────→ .7 ──┘
              .6 → .8 ─┘
```

`bdi-2bb.3` is the head of the TUI: it lands the module skeleton with real
signatures — every module created and declared in `src/view/mod.rs`, plus the
domain-action enum — so nothing after it edits a file another bead is holding.
That is what lets `.4`, `.5` and `.6` all run at once. `bdi-2bb.9` needs
nothing and can start immediately beside it.

`bdi-z0d → bdi-1a6` ran alongside and is closed. `bdi-7ph` continued it and
has moved to `bdi-iby`.

The live critical path is now `bdi-2bb.21` and `bdi-2bb.22` → `bdi-2bb.1` →
`bdi-2bb` → the epic. The tracker-resolution epic `bdi-7ao.15` (`.13`, `.14`)
runs alongside and touches `config.rs` and the bd runner, not the view.

---

## File ownership — seats share one working tree

There are no worktrees here; concurrent seats edit the same checkout, so two
beads owning one file is a collision, not a merge. This map is why several
edges above exist:

| File | Owner |
|---|---|
| `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `src/lib.rs` | `bdi-2bb.3` **only** — any bead wanting a dependency or a module routes back here |
| `src/main.rs` | `bdi-wf5` → `bdi-ijq` → `bdi-2bb.6`, in that order |
| `src/config.rs` | `bdi-wf5`, then `bdi-2bb.6` |
| `src/model/snapshot.rs` | `bdi-2bb.9` — **and no one else**; `bdi-2bb.4` and `bdi-ijq` were both drawn toward it and were re-shaped to stay out |
| `src/app.rs` | `bdi-wf5`, then `bdi-ijq` |
| `src/collect/herdr.rs`, `src/collect/run.rs` | `bdi-2bb.2` |
| `src/view/mod.rs`, `src/view/row.rs` | `bdi-2bb.3` |
| `src/view/forest.rs` | `bdi-2bb.4` |
| `src/view/tail.rs` | `bdi-2bb.7` — created and declared as a stub by `bdi-2bb.3` |
| `src/view/draw.rs` | `bdi-2bb.5`, then `bdi-2bb.7` at its stub points |
| `src/tui.rs` | `bdi-2bb.6`, then `bdi-2bb.7` at its stub points |
| `flake.nix` | `bdi-z0d` |
| `.github/` | `bdi-1a6` |
| `docs/design.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | `bdi-2bb.1`, and `bdi-2bb.8` for the protocol. `bdi-8df` borrows `CLAUDE.md` for one clause and hands it back |
| `README.md` | `bdi-2bb.8` |

`bdi-2bb.7`'s two edits into `draw.rs` and `tui.rs` are the only files any bead
shares with another, which is why it is wired behind both rather than beside
them. Everything not listed here — `tests/`, `docs/plans/` — is unowned, so a
seat needing one should say so rather than assume it is free.

**These seven children are the TUI's plan.** `CLAUDE.md` says the TUI "gets its
own plan, written against the real types"; this is it. There is no
`docs/plans/` document for it and none is expected — the core's plan was wrong
in all eleven of its task listings, and writing the next one as beads against
the landed types is the correction.

---

## Constraints every seat inherits, proved on the core

- **No bd or herdr error text reaches the screen verbatim.** bd's auth failure
  names the database and the SQL user. The model carries a failure *kind*; the
  renderer says the words. `bdi-2bb.3` is where those words get written.
- **Test data is fictional.** `tests/fixtures/` stays a faithful capture of
  this machine's own session; everything inline is invented. `bdi-ifn` scrubbed
  83 real identifiers out of the core's tests — don't put them back.
- **Mutation-test before trusting a green.** Every seat on the core found a
  real hole this way. `cargo-mutants` is not in the dev shell but *is* reachable
  with no flake change — `nix develop --command nix shell nixpkgs#cargo-mutants
  --command cargo-mutants mutants --file <path>`, nested so the toolchain still
  comes from the dev shell. Note the `mutants` subcommand: without it the binary
  prints cargo's usage, which reads exactly like "not installed". Hand-applying
  a chosen mutant is still the right tool when you have a specific property in
  mind; a sweep is for finding what you did not think of. `bdi-7ao.11` holds the
  open question of pinning it and whether a sweep becomes a gate.
- **Run the mutation harness under a memory ceiling**, because a deleted cycle
  guard is a plausible mutant and an unbounded loop took 15.7 GiB in under two
  minutes:
  `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=4G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -q -- cargo test …`
  `MemorySwapMax=0` is load-bearing — with 68 GiB of swap, `MemoryMax` alone
  thrashes instead of killing. Do **not** use `ulimit -v`: it caps address
  space, which Rust reserves per thread, so it produces false kills that read
  exactly like killed mutants.
- **Question the brief.** Every seat on the core found its task listing wrong.
  A brief that does not match the code is a defect in the brief.
- **An unlanded branch is `wip_branch` / `wip_commit` metadata on the bead**,
  never a note. Metadata is single-valued, so there is one answer and it is the
  current one; appended notes leave a stale SHA standing above a fresh one, and
  a top-down reader hits the stale one first. It also makes the work findable
  from cold: `bd list --has-metadata-key wip_branch --limit 0 --json`.

---

## Two decisions Graeme made on 2026-08-30, mid-prep

**1. `docs/design.md` is a starting point, not gospel.** We deviate as we learn
and get into the details. This supersedes `CLAUDE.md`'s line that the design
*"is accepted; changes to it are design decisions, not edits."* `bdi-8df`
replaced that line with this rule, so the repo and the anchor now say the same
thing. In practice: where the design is ambiguous, the seat that hits the
ambiguity decides it with the code in front of it and records what it chose;
`bdi-2bb.1` folds those into the document at the end. Every such question is
already written into the bead that owns it, with a recommended default.

Its known drift, for the same bead: the JSON example (~lines 451–476) shows
`"anomaly": null` where the model emits `anomalies: []`, and its `unattributed`
entry lacks the `project` field the model carries. The prose governs and the
code already follows it.

**2. Refresh is a capability, not a fixed poll.** The design says refresh is a
poll *because herdr has no event stream* — true of herdr, not of bd. So `bdi`
detects a change-notification source per project, uses it where one exists, and
falls back to a timer where none does. `bdi-2bb.6` builds the seam and the
timer; `bdi-2bb.8` adds the source.

**And the source is an interface, not a built-in watcher** — any process can
tell `bdi` a project changed, and a setup wires whatever it has. That holds the
line this project was designed under: `bdi` knows nothing about how a setup is
organised. It is also forced by the facts. The assistant project's mechanism
(`#assistant/bd-change-notification`, 2026-08-30) is Dolt's binlog consumed as
a GTID stream, which needs a replication user and a unique `server_id` —
server-level privileges beady-eye's DB-scoped tenant user does not have and
should not require of anyone else — and Dolt multiplexes every tenant onto one
stream, so a built-in consumer would receive row data for trackers the user
never asked to watch. Behind a socket, that consumer needs nothing from `bdi`
and `bdi` needs nothing from the cluster.

**Workers close when done and new work gets a fresh seat.** Graeme's rule,

worker.

## What Graeme asked for, and the chain that delivers it

`bdi-7ao.22` — run `bdi` under a watcher so a running copy picks up changes — is
**P1 and is what he actually wants**. It is dep-blocked on `bdi-7ao.21`, and the
reason is written into it: watchexec restarts by killing `bdi`, so until a signal
restores the terminal every rebuild hands him a trap. So `.21` is the critical
path, not a P2 bug.

**The signal fault is measured, not inferred.** SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP each
leave six DEC private modes set — `?1049h ?1000h ?1002h ?1003h ?1015h ?1006h` —
plus the cursor hidden, with **zero bytes written after the signal**. Quitting
with `q` emits the exact reverse. So `Drop` already restores the complete set:
**the fix routes signals through `Drop` and must not grow its own mode list**,
which would rot when crossterm changes what `EnableMouseCapture` sets.

Recovery for a terminal left in that state:
`printf '\033[?1006l\033[?1015l\033[?1003l\033[?1002l\033[?1000l\033[?25h'; stty sane; tput rmcup`

**`bdi-7ao.26` — the TUI never clears on startup — is independent by
construction and must not be closed as a duplicate of `.21`.** Measured: after a
**SIGKILL** (uncatchable, so no signal handling can prevent it) the next run
emits no erase sequence at all and leaves **1612 of 4800 cells untouched, 33.6%**,
on a 120x40 screen. Stale text survives in the gaps, which is why it reads as
intermittent. One `terminal.clear()` after init in `Screen::showing`
(`src/tui.rs:735`) fixes it permanently. Held behind `.21` for landing order in
the same function, not because the bug depends on it.

## Dependency edges added 2026-08-31 10:00, and why

`bdi-sw4`, `bdi-7ao.20`, `bdi-2bb.22`, `bdi-2bb.24`, `bdi-7ao.23` and
`bdi-7ao.12` are all **blocked by `bdi-7ao.24`**, which is rewriting their
descriptions right now against the landed row types. Spawning onto a bead whose
description is mid-correction is how a seat builds from a stale premise — which
nearly retired three beads today. They release when `.24` closes.

**`bdi-sw4` is NOT settled by the split.** The `bdi-2bb.25` seat claimed it was
and withdrew the claim. Its premise is a colour measurement on Graeme's
terminal: `themes/noctalia.conf` sets `foreground` and `color15` to the same
`#ede0da`, so `\e[38;5;15m` and `\e[39m` collapse exactly. Nothing in the split
changes which SGR codes are emitted. A staffed root now sits on that scale too,
so the bug has **one more row on it** than before.

**`bdi-7ao.24` is the pass over the parked beads**, blocked by `bdi-2bb.25`.
Their descriptions do not go stale gradually — they become wrong at that one
sha. Do not spawn it early; the dep edge holds it out of `bd ready`.

## Filed from Graeme's drops, 2026-08-31 10:15 BST

Four beads opened from things Graeme said in passing. Each is wired, none is
staffed, and the edges are why — not seat budget.

| bead | what | held by |
|---|---|---|
| `bdi-7ao.26` | The TUI never clears on startup — **measured, independent of `.21`** | `bdi-7ao.21` (landing order in `Screen::showing`) |
| `bdi-7ao.27` | `Snapshot::generated_at` says *now* for a project that was not re-read | `bdi-2bb.21` |
| `bdi-7ao.28` | Run `/misplaced-emphasis` over `CLAUDE.md` | `bdi-n1m` |
| `bdi-ev3` | **Spike:** embed a live herdr pane rather than redrawing its text | nothing — spawnable |

**`bdi-7ao.27` is a published-contract defect, not a view nicety.**
`generated_at` is in the JSON contract (`tests/snapshot_json.rs:121`), and
projects collect serially over `cfg.projects` filtered by `wanted` — so a
`Wanted::Project` refresh leaves every skipped project untouched while
`generated_at` is set to `now`. The Noctalia widget waits behind that contract,
so a consumer would draw freshness wrong with no way to know. Wired behind
`bdi-2bb.21` because that seat is settling view-wide vs per-project, which very
likely resolves it.

**`bdi-ev3` is post-v1 and deliberately not parented here.** Graeme asked for a
spike on embedding a real herdr panel, interactive if possible, *"but if not,
live read-only would still be useful"*. The useful finding already in the bead:
`herdr agent read` takes `--format text|ansi` and `bdi` passes `text`
(`src/collect/herdr.rs:50`), which is why it reads as content redrawn. The
read-only half may be close to a format change plus an ANSI-to-spans parser.
**The interactive half breaks a stated property** — `CLAUDE.md:4` says bdi is
read-only, and sending keys into another agent's pane is a write. The spike
surfaces that for Graeme rather than deciding it.

## Cost model for a collection, superseding the single number

Measured twice today. `93fb2c4` added a **second `bd` subprocess per project**
(`bd query` for wisps, which `bd list` does not return), and it landed *after*
the first reading — so the two disagree for a reason:

| | before `93fb2c4` | at `40f4eb5` |
|---|---|---|
| beady-eye alone | 0.61-0.70 s | 1.11-1.48 s |
| summit-works alone | 2.02-2.48 s | 2.31-2.44 s |
| both, as Graeme runs them | 2.49-2.71 s | 3.49-4.10 s |

Only the small tracker moved, which is the tell: cost is now substantially
**per-project fixed**, not per-row. A config with four projects pays roughly
four times that regardless of size. `src/config.rs:87-95` still records
9.4-11.2 s and is wrong; `bdi-2bb.21` is correcting it. `bdi-2bb.23` owns the
30 s interval and now rests on a cost model with a per-project term.

Amends the held-back note above, 08:50 BST 2026-08-31: **worktrees weaken the
contention argument, and seats moved into them this morning.**

`bdi-2bb.25` is on branch `root-row-agent` in its own worktree, `bdi-7ao.14` on
`wip/tracker-env` in its own, and `bdi-7ao.17` commits from the main checkout and
then removes its build sandbox. Measured cause, from the `bdi-7ao.17` seat: another
seat's half-finished `src/view/phrase.rs` stopped the *shared* tree compiling, so
`cargo test` there told it nothing about its own code. `bdi-2bb.25` ran `cargo test`
twice in the shared tree, got green, and that green was about four seats' work.

**So the reason to hold a bead is no longer "another seat holds that file".** It is
only the landing order — whoever lands second rebases onto a rename or an argv
change they could not read. That is cheap for a mechanical change and expensive for
a semantic one, and the two seats sharing `src/collect/bd.rs` sorted it between
themselves in their own topics rather than needing the orchestrator.

Practical effect for the next orchestrator: `bdi-2bb.22`, `bdi-2bb.24` and `bdi-sw4`
are spawnable now if each seat takes a worktree, rather than waiting on `.25` and
`.21` to land. `bdi-7ao.12` still wants to run alone — not for contention but because
it rewrites ~200 fixture rows across seven files, so every seat that lands after it
rebases onto a changed fixture shape.

The repo supports this: `.envrc` resolves `.env.local` and `.envrc.local` from
`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`'s parent, so a worktree gets the tracker and the
credential. Checked from a worktree by the `bdi-2bb.25` seat, not assumed.

title: T1 scaffold the crate, extending the existing dev shell
description:
Plan: Task 1, `docs/plans/2026-08-30-core-and-json.md:25`.

**Deliverable:** crate `beady_eye` (lib) plus binary `bdi`, building and
testing under the existing dev shell. Every later task adds modules under
`src/`.

## Two corrections to the plan, both load-bearing

**Extend `flake.nix`; do not create it.** The plan says "Create: flake.nix"
and gives a bare Rust shell. `flake.nix` already exists and carries the beads
1.2.2 pin, `BEADS_DIR`, `BD_SMART_GATE=0` and the `.env.local` sourcing.
Replacing it breaks the tracker for every session. Add cargo, rustc, rustfmt,
clippy and rust-analyzer to the existing `buildInputs`, and add the
`packages.default` rustPlatform derivation alongside the existing devShell. Do
not add `inputs.nixpkgs.follows` to the beads input — the flake's own comment
says why.

**Do not create `rust-toolchain.toml`.** The plan pins channel 1.83 there
while the shell supplies nixpkgs' rustc. There is no rustup on this machine,
so the file is inert at best, and actively fights the flake if rustup ever
lands on PATH. The flake is the pin.

## Definition of done

- `cargo test` passes `version_is_not_empty`.
- `cargo run` prints `bdi 0.1.0`.
- **Still works after the change:** `nix develop` prints the beads version and
  its resolved path, loads `.env.local`, and `bd list` reaches the tracker from
  inside the shell. Confirm this, don't assume it — the flake edit is the one
  place this effort can break the tracker it is tracked in.
- Committed and pushed.

title: Core and --json: read bd and herdr, emit the contract
description:
Effort slug: `core-json`

## Goal

A `bdi --json` binary that reads one or more beads trackers and, where
available, a herdr session, and emits a tree of work per root annotated with
the live agent on each node. The TUI and the Noctalia widget are out of scope
and get their own plans.

## The plan

`docs/plans/2026-08-30-core-and-json.md`. `docs/design.md` is the spec and is
accepted; where the plan and the design disagree, the design wins.

**The plan has a Known defects section at its end.** Each entry names the task
it lands in, and every one is folded into the relevant bead. A worker that
implements its plan task verbatim will reproduce a known bug. **Read the
bead's corrections before the plan's code.**

## Roster

Eleven beads, all in this tracker. No foreign strands, no tracking beads.

| bead | task | blocked by |
|---|---|---|
| bdi-3um.1 | T1 scaffold the crate, extending the existing dev shell | — |
| bdi-3um.2 | T2 configuration, with the per-project credential command | .1 |
| bdi-3um.3 | T3 parse bd's dependency-tree JSON | .1 |
| bdi-3um.5 | T5 parse herdr's agent list | .1 |
| bdi-3um.4 | T4 assemble and order the tree | .3 |
| bdi-3um.6 | T6 join agents onto beads, scoped by project | .2 .4 .5 |
| bdi-3um.9 | T9 run bd and herdr per project, per-project credential | .2 .5 |
| bdi-3um.7 | T7 anomaly rules, every rule that fires | .6 |
| bdi-3um.8 | T8 assemble the snapshot, counts, live-agent filter | .7 |
| bdi-3um.10 | T10 wire the binary and emit the JSON contract | .8 .9 |
| bdi-3um.11 | T11 discovery rule 4: roots named only by a live pane | .10 |

`.11` is not in the plan. It carries discovery rule 4, split out of `.10`,
which was otherwise carrying app wiring, discovery, a snapshot-type change and
an integration test in one bead.

`.5` does not block on `.3`, despite the plan's numbering. It consumes nothing
from it; the only coupling is a two-line `src/collect/mod.rs`.

## Critical path and parallel windows

`.1` → `.3` → `.4` → `.6` → `.7` → `.8` → `.10` → `.11`.

`.9` opens once `.2` and `.5` are done and runs alongside the whole
`.6` → `.7` → `.8` chain. That is the effort's one long parallel strand.

## Delivery mode: direct push

`main` on `github.com/CodeForBreakfast/beady-eye` reports `protected: false`
and has no rulesets. **Beads close on push, not on merge.** No PR-ordering
edges are wired, because there is no review tower to prevent.

## How concurrent seats work in this repo

**Seats share one working tree** — `/tmp/bdi-ground/beady-eye`. They
are not worktrees.

- **Stage per path.** `git add <specific files>`, never `git add -A`. A seat
  that stages broadly commits another seat's half-finished work.
- **Expect another seat's code to be present.** A `pub mod` line you were about
  to add may already be there, and files you do not own will be modified around
  you. Build failures from a neighbour's in-flight code are transient.
- **Worktrees are not a drop-in alternative.** They fix build isolation but a
  worktree can only deliver to main with `git push <branch>:main`. Do not move
  a seat to a worktree without checking that its push actually works first.

**If a seat cannot push, stand it down and respawn a fresh seat on the same
bead.** One seat had every writing git command refused — `git push`, including
a guaranteed-no-op bare push on an up-to-date main, and `git merge --ff-only` —
while read-only git (fetch, log, status, diff, rev-list) worked throughout, and
while other seats pushed fine from the same directory in the same hour. The
denial is scoped to the seat, not to the repo, the branch or the refspec.
Recovery is cheap because the commit already lives on a branch in the shared
repo.

## Finding spawnable work

`bd ready --exclude-type=epic`. This epic is unblocked and so appears in a bare
`bd ready`; it is the anchor, not work.

## Facts verified against the live tracker

Established during prep and corrected by `bdi-3um.3`'s capture. These override
any contradicting reading of `docs/design.md`'s data-sources table.

- **`bd dep tree --json` omits empty fields.** `edge_from_parent`, `metadata`,
  `closed_at` and `close_reason` are *absent*, not null, when empty. A parser
  written against one row shape breaks on the first real tracker.
- **`parent_id` on the root is an empty string, not an absent field.**
  `bdi-3um.3` normalises it to `None` at the parse boundary.
- **`bd dep tree --direction=up` walks *dependents* — what the issue blocks —
  not ancestors.** bd's own `--help` says so, and `bdi-3um.10` measured it:
  asked about `bdi-3um.10` it returns two rows, `bdi-3um.10` itself with
  `parent_id: ""` and the bead it blocks beneath it. Whatever bead it is asked
  about comes back as its own root, however deep that bead sits.
- **`parent_id` in dep-tree output is the *traversal* parent, not the bead's
  own.** In the default direction from `bdi-3um.10`, the epic `bdi-3um` comes
  back as a child of `bdi-3um.8` over a `parent-child` edge. So no dep-tree
  answer can be walked upward to find a root.
- **`bd show <id> --json` is the only call carrying the real parent.** The
  field is `parent` — not `parent_id` — a bare id string, `null` on a root, and
  the array-not-object note in `docs/design.md` is right. Walking it one level
  at a time is how a bead reaches the top of its parent-child chain, which is
  what the design's discovery rules 1 and 2 require. `bdi-3um.10` implements
  that walk as `app::root_of`, memoised per project and guarded against a
  parent chain that loops.
- **`assignee` and `started_at` are present on a claimed bead.** They are still
  optional, so nothing in the design changes, but they are real: `.7`'s age
  rules and `.8`'s emission both want them.
- **`metadata` is inline per row** — confirmed on a bead carrying `agent_pane`.
  The design is right: badges need no second call.
- **`blocked_by` is NOT recoverable from `bd dep tree`.** A node with two
  blockers appears once, under one of them; the other is absent entirely.
  `bd blocked --json` is the source — it returns `blocked_by: [ids]` and
  `blocked_by_count`. `.9` delivers it, `.8` consumes it.
- **`bd show` cannot tell an id it does not hold from a dead server.**
  Measured by `.11` on 2026-08-30: `bd show "reviewing the docs" --json`
  exits **1**, printing `no issue found matching "reviewing the docs"` on
  stderr and `{"error": "no issues found matching the provided IDs"}` — a
  JSON *object*, not the array a success returns. That stderr carries neither
  an auth phrase nor an unreachable one, so `RunFailure::from_exit` falls to
  its catch-all and classifies it **`FailureKind::Unavailable`** — the same
  kind a refused connection produces. Consequence, and it is what forces
  discovery rule 4's shape: a lookup on free text has **no failure kind to
  discriminate on**, so rule 4 swallows its failure unconditionally. There is
  no cleverer version available at that layer, and a heuristic on stderr text
  would breach the no-bd-error-text rule to reach one.
- **`RunFailure::from_exit`'s catch-all is `Unavailable`.** Any bd failure
  nobody classified arrives looking like an outage. A property of the shipped
  classifier rather than of any one caller; the TUI will meet it again.
- **Sibling order from bd is arbitrary.** The root's children came back
  `.10, .7, .2, .5, .3, .1`. Re-ordering in `.4` is load-bearing.
- `bdi-5yq`, the closed smoke-test bead, carries an `agent_pane` metadata key
  so a metadata-bearing row can be captured for a fixture. Leave it set.

## File ownership where beads run concurrently

`.8` and `.9` run in parallel and both need `TrackerState`'s unreachable
reason. Resolved by ownership, not an edge: `.9` detects failures in its own
`collect/run.rs`, `.8` defines the representation in `snapshot.rs`, `.10` maps
between them. Neither reaches into the other's file.

## The join conflicts have a sink

`docs/design.md` says the four join disagreements are *reported*, but its JSON
contract has nowhere to put them — so as written `.6` computes findings that
`.8` drops. They are carried as a top-level **`conflicts`** list on the
snapshot, mirroring `unattributed`, which is the existing precedent for a
finding belonging to no tree. Open to reversal if Graeme wants another shape.

## The effort's deferred risk

`bdi-vx7` — prove the per-project credential against a live second tracker.
`.9` tests that path against a `Runner` fake only, by design. `bdi-vx7` is
deliberately outside this effort and blocked, because it needs a cross-project
consent decision that is Graeme's. **Do not staff it.**

## A live defect found by this effort, decided and staffed

`bdi-91d` (P1) — a config mixing a credentialled project with an ambient one
leaks the first project's `BEADS_DOLT_PASSWORD` to the second, because the
shell already exports it. Graeme chose: **`credential_command` is required on
every project once the config names more than one**; a single-project config
still needs none. `credential_command` stays `Option<String>` — the fix is a
validation rule in `src/config.rs`, not a type change. Distinct from
`bdi-vx7`, which is about proving the path, not about which configs are legal.

## Global constraints, on every bead

- **Never write to bd.** Only `list`, `show`, `dep tree`, `ready`, `blocked`.
  Only `herdr agent list` / `read` / `get`.
- **The key is `(project, id)`, never `id` alone.** Prefixes are per-tracker
  and uncoordinated.
- **Degrade, never disappear.** An unreachable tracker, a dangling parent, a
  truncated subtree, a filtered tree — each is reported, never dropped.
- **`--limit 0` on every `bd list`.** Measured: `bd ready` takes `-n/--limit`
  and its default is **100**, `0` meaning unlimited. `bd blocked` has **no
  `--limit` flag at all** (only `--parent`), so the rule does not apply to it.
  Truncation silently changes meaning, so pass it wherever it exists.
- **Mutation-test before trusting a green.** The plan's own tests repeatedly
  pass against a wrong implementation: T2 asserted defaults for sections its
  fixture omitted, T4 shipped the expected depths in its fixture and exercised
  its cycle guard on a disconnected component, T6 asserts on ids and an
  `agent_pane` value present in no captured fixture. Change the implementation
  to be wrong and confirm a test fails. Every seat that has done it found a
  real hole.
- **Cap the mutation harness's memory, not its wall clock.** A mutant that
  deletes a loop's terminating condition does not fail — it allocates until the
  machine notices. One reached **15.7 GiB, 24% of RAM**, before a shell timeout
  cut it; a wall-clock cap ends the run but lets the machine suffer for its
  whole length. Measured on this machine, exit 137 on a runaway and clean
  completion under the same cap:

  ```
  systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=4G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -q -- cargo test ...
  ```

  `MemorySwapMax=0` is load-bearing: this box has 68 GiB of swap, so
  `MemoryMax` alone thrashes instead of killing. Prefer this to `ulimit -v`,
  which caps address space rather than resident memory and trips on the space
  Rust reserves per thread — spurious failures unrelated to the mutant.
  Non-termination is a normal mutation-testing outcome, so the harness has to
  survive it without anyone outside the run noticing.
- **herdr's `agent_status` is a terminal property**, never a bead status and
  never a badge.
- **Fail loudly on an unexpected JSON shape.** A field of the wrong type is an
  error; a *missing* field is normal — see the omitempty finding above.
- **Test data is fictional; fixtures are real.** Graeme's rule, 2026-08-30.
  Inline and hand-built test data uses invented ids, project names, paths,
  pane ids and hostnames — never this tracker's beads, this machine's panes,
  `/tmp/bdi-ground/…` or a real host. The two files under `tests/fixtures/`
  stay faithful captures, because their job is to pin the real wire shape and
  `CLAUDE.md` requires it. So: real shape, invented content, and the
  distinction is the file it lives in. Keep parsing real — build test beads by
  running invented JSON through `parse_dep_tree`, not by struct literal.
- **TDD with a real red phase.** Write the test, watch it fail for the right
  reason, then implement. Missing module wiring is not a red phase.

## Working in this repo

`nix develop` (or direnv) — it pins bd 1.2.2 and scopes `BEADS_DIR`. A bare
`bd` from an ambient shell may resolve a different binary or another project's
tracker. See `CLAUDE.md`.

title: T11 discovery rule 4: roots named only by a live pane
description:
Split out of bdi-3um.10 during prep, which was carrying too much for one
context. This is new work — the plan's Task 10 does not implement it and does
not consult `panes` at all. Its self-review claimed full spec coverage and was
wrong.

**Deliverable:** the fourth root source in `docs/design.md`'s Discovery
section — a bead named by a live pane's `display_agent` that rules 1 to 3
missed, unioned and deduped into the root set.

## Why it exists

So an agent working off-tree still appears. It is the only root herdr
contributes; every other root comes from bd, which is deliberate — an earlier
draft had herdr enumerate the roots and that drops any root with no pane,
silently and with concrete evidence behind it.

## Watch for

- `display_agent` is **free text**. Any string an agent stamps lands there, so
  parsing it as a bead id is a heuristic and must fail soft: a value that is
  not a resolvable bead id contributes no root and is not an error.
- The pane must resolve to a project first (bdi-3um.6's rule), and the root it
  contributes belongs to that project. `(project, id)`, never id alone.

## What bdi-3um.10 landed, against which this wires

`src/app.rs`. `run(cfg, runner, filter, now) -> Snapshot` fetches the panes
once, before the project loop, then calls `read_project(runner, project, cfg)`
per project. `read_project` builds that project's root set and returns its
readiness and one entry per root. **Rule 4 needs the panes inside
`read_project`, so that signature grows a `panes` argument — it is the only
one that changes.**

- The root set is a `BTreeSet<String>`, so a bead rules 1 to 3 already found
  dedups by itself. Nothing has to ask whether the other rules missed it.
- `join::project_of(&pane.cwd, &cfg.projects)` places a pane in its project;
  `run` already calls it for `unattributed`. A pane under no configured
  project contributes no root.
- `root_of(runner, project, env, id, ancestors)` walks `bd show <id> --json`'s
  `parent` field one level at a time — see the anchor's measured bd facts for
  why no `bd dep tree` answer can do this. Reuse it, and pass the same
  `ancestors` map, so a pane-named bead under an already-walked epic costs one
  call rather than a fresh climb.

**The trap, and it is the whole reason this needs care.** `read_project`
propagates every `root_of` failure with `?`, which makes it the project's
failure — a `FailedProject` with no trees at all. That is right for a bead bd
itself named in discovery, and wrong for a `display_agent`. A pane labelled
`reviewing the docs` would make `bd show` fail and take the whole tracker's
output down with it. **Rule 4's lookup must swallow its own failure and
contribute nothing**, which is the fail-soft requirement above stated in terms
of the code that exists.

A rule-4 tree has a live agent by construction, so `Filter::LiveAgents` never
hides one.

## Definition of done

- A pane whose `display_agent` names a bead no other rule found produces that
  bead's root in the output.
- A pane whose `display_agent` is not a bead id changes nothing and raises
  nothing.
- **Still true:** rules 1 to 3 produce the same roots they did before, and a
  root with no pane at all still appears.
- A real red phase, then implement.
- Committed and pushed.
close_reason: Discovery rule 4 landed in 86cd807. read_project takes panes; a pane placed in this project by join::project_of contributes its display_agent's root, climbed with the shared ancestors memo and deduped in the existing BTreeSet. The lookup swallows its failure unconditionally, because bd cannot distinguish an id it does not hold from a dead server — measured and recorded on the anchor. 167 tests green, clippy and fmt clean, nix build green. Nine mutants applied: eight killed, one proved equivalent.

title: T10 wire the binary and emit the JSON contract
description:
Plan: Task 10, `docs/plans/2026-08-30-core-and-json.md:1990`.

**Deliverable:** `app::run`, `root_of`, the per-project loop, `bdi --json`,
`bdi --config <path>`, `bdi --all`, and `tests/snapshot_json.rs`.

**Discovery rule 4 is not in this bead** — it is bdi-3um.11, which depends on
this one. Implement rules 1 to 3 here and leave the seam for it.

## What this bead wires together

- Per project: build the environment from `credential_command` (bdi-3um.2),
  run the collectors (bdi-3um.9), and map a `collect::run` failure onto the
  `TrackerState` reason that bdi-3um.8 defines. **This mapping is this bead's
  job** — `.8` and `.9` deliberately never touch each other's files.
- Feed `ready_ids` and `blocked_by` from bdi-3um.9 into `build_tree`. Those
  are the only sources; nothing infers readiness or a blocker set.
- Emit the contract.

## The model bdi-3um.8 landed (`2a85279`), against which this wires

`model::snapshot` is written, tested and pushed. Its shape, so this bead is not
re-derived from the plan, whose Task 8 listing is stale in every particular:

    build_tree(project, &Assembled, &Joined, &Readiness, &Config, now) -> Tree
    build(Collected, panes, &Joined, &Config, HerdrState, Filter, now) -> Snapshot

- **`join::resolve` is called once, across every project**, before any tree is
  built. `build_tree` never resolves; it looks agents up by
  `BeadKey { project, id }`. So the loop collects every project's `Assembled`
  first, resolves once over all of them, then builds each tree.
- **`Readiness { ready: BTreeSet<String>, blocked_by: BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> }`**
  is where `bd::ready_ids` and `bd::blocked_by` go, per project.
- **`Collected { trees: Vec<Tree>, failed_projects: Vec<FailedProject> }`** is
  one outcome per configured project.
- **The failure mapping this bead owns** is `collect::run::FailureKind` onto
  `snapshot::TrackerFailure`, variant for variant: `Auth`, `Unavailable`,
  `Exec`, `Parse`. `TrackerFailure` is a kind and carries no text at all, so
  `RunFailure.detail` is dropped here rather than rendered — the words for a
  failure belong to whatever draws it.
- **Two shapes of tracker failure, and this bead chooses between them.** A root
  already discovered whose `bd dep tree` failed is
  `Tree::tracker_unreachable(project, root, failure)` — it keeps its id, has no
  nodes, and the filter never hides it. A project whose discovery itself failed
  has no root to name, and is a `FailedProject { project, tracker }` instead.
- **`LoosePane` carries `project: Option<String>`** beside `cwd`, so a consumer
  groups loose panes under a failed project without re-running `project_of`.
  This is additive to the design's example, which shows `pane`, `cwd` and
  `pane_status` only.
- **`Snapshot` does not carry `Joined`**, which has no `Serialize` on purpose:
  `BTreeMap<BeadKey, _>` compiles and then fails at runtime as a JSON map key.
  `conflicts` is `Joined.conflicts`, cloned onto the snapshot.

## Known defects to fix as you reach them

**`the_json_carries_the_contract_fields` asserts key presence only**, so nulls
and wrong enum spellings pass. Assert values.

**The node's field is `anomalies`, a list.** `docs/design.md`'s JSON example
still shows `"anomaly": null`, and its `unattributed` entry has no `project`.
Both are stale against the design's own prose, which governs; the model follows
the prose.

## Definition of done

- `bdi --json` emits the contract in `docs/design.md` — `generated_at`,
  `herdr`, `filter`, `trees`, `hidden_trees`, `unattributed` — plus the
  top-level `conflicts` list that bdi-3um.8 adds so the join findings have
  somewhere to go.
- `agent.source` records which direction of the join resolved each agent;
  `herdr` is `ok` or `unavailable` so a consumer knows which tier it reads.
- A project whose tracker is unreachable renders as its own failure, named,
  with its live panes — not as an anonymous empty tree, and two such failures
  stay distinguishable.
- Roots come from bd, unioned and deduped across discovery rules 1 to 3.
- **Still true at the end:** the binary never writes to bd. No bd subcommand
  beyond `list`, `show`, `dep tree`, `ready`, `blocked`; no herdr subcommand
  beyond `agent list`. `agent focus` belongs to the TUI, not here.
- A real red phase, then implement.
- Committed and pushed.

title: T4 assemble and order the tree
description:
Plan: Task 4, `docs/plans/2026-08-30-core-and-json.md:570`.

**Deliverable:** `model::tree::{Placed, Assembled, assemble}` — rows into a
renderable structure by `parent_id`, siblings re-ordered, depth recomputed
from the parent chain.

bd has already resolved and deduped the tree, so this assembles rows; it does
not walk edges.

## Known defects to fix as you reach them

**`assemble` silently keeps only the last root.** `None => root = Some(bead)`
overwrites. Valid `bd dep tree` output has exactly one root — validate that
and fail loudly rather than discarding components.

**Unreachable rows are dropped.** Rows not reached by the traversal must be
reported alongside `dangling`. Degrade, never disappear, applies to them too.

## Three tests that would pass against a wrong implementation

Fix these as you write them, not after:

- `depth_is_recomputed_from_the_parent_chain` — the plan's fixture already
  carries the expected `depth` values, so simply copying bd's `depth` passes.
  Give the fixture deliberately wrong depths.
- `a_parent_cycle_terminates` — `b` and `c` are disconnected, so `walk` never
  reaches them and the `seen` guard is never exercised. Wire the cycle into
  the reachable graph.
- `siblings_order_...` — it tests the status rank and neither the priority nor
  the id tie-break. Assert all three.

## Definition of done

- `assemble` returns `Assembled { rows, dangling, unreachable }` from a flat
  `Vec<Bead>`: one row per bead, in render order, each with a depth recomputed
  from its parent chain rather than copied from bd.
- **Sibling order is state, then priority, then id** — in-flight, then
  blocked, then open, then closed; then priority; then id. All three tie-breaks
  asserted.
- Exactly one root, or a loud failure.
- A parent id naming a bead not in the input is reported as `dangling`, never
  dropped; a row the traversal never reaches is reported as `unreachable`.
- A cycle in the parent chain terminates rather than hanging.
- A real red phase: write the test, watch it fail *for the right reason*, then
  implement. Missing module wiring is not a red phase.
- Committed and pushed.

## Note on the real data

`bd dep tree` returns rows in a valid pre-order but with **arbitrary sibling
order** — verified on this repo's own tracker, where the root's children came
back `.10, .7, .2, .5, .3, .1`. Re-ordering is the whole point of this bead;
do not assume bd's order is already what you want.
notes:
From bdi-3um.3's live capture, 2026-08-30: bd emits parent_id as an EMPTY STRING on the root row, not as an absent field. docs/design.md:203 says the same. bdi-3um.3 normalises empty-string to None at the parse boundary, so this bead should never see Some(""). If it ever does, the root gets filed as a dangling parent — that is the bug this note exists to prevent. Do not re-add a plain Option<String> passthrough.
From bdi-3um.3, measured on this tracker 2026-08-30: 'bd dep tree <root> --direction=up --json --max-depth=N' does NOT mark deep nodes truncated — it REPARENTS them. At --max-depth=2, bdi-3um.4, .9 and .11 came back at depth 1 with parent_id rewritten to bdi-3um, their real parents gone. So a depth-limited call returns a DIFFERENT TREE, not a marked-incomplete one, and recomputing depth from the parent chain cannot recover the real shape because parent_id was rewritten too. Practical upshot for bdi-3um.9: DO NOT pass --max-depth when invoking bd. Practical upshot for bdi-3um.4: recomputing depth from the parent chain is correct, and this is the evidence for it; Bead deliberately carries no depth field. Second-order: no live row ever sets truncated, which is why bdi-3um.3's truncated assertion uses an inline literal rather than a captured row.
close_reason:
model::tree::{Placed, Assembled, assemble} landed as e847648, pushed to main. 11 tests, real red phase (all 11 failed on assertions against an empty stub, not on module wiring). Full suite 30 pass, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt clean, nix build .#default produces a working bdi.

All three known defects fixed: exactly one root or a loud failure naming the offending ids; unreachable rows reported AND kept; depth counted from the parent chain.

Two corrections to the brief, both accepted by the orchestrator. (1) Bead carries no depth field at all — bdi-3um.3 dropped it at the parse boundary — so the 'copies bd's depth' false green is structurally impossible; the test asserts recomputation against an inline row set with deliberately wrong depth values rather than corrupting the captured fixture. (2) With single-parent pointers a cycle CANNOT be wired into the reachable graph: a node in a cycle has its parent inside the cycle, so the component is always disjoint from the root. What makes the seen guard load-bearing is the unreachable fix — keeping those rows forces the walk to enter the cycle. The two known defects are one defect.

Signature change from the plan (assemble returns Result) is noted on bdi-3um.6.

title: T3 parse bd's dependency-tree JSON
description:
Plan: Task 3, `docs/plans/2026-08-30-core-and-json.md:354`.

**Deliverable:** `model::types::{Bead, Status, Edge}`,
`collect::bd::parse_dep_tree`, and the `tests/fixtures/bd_dep_tree.json`
fixture.

## Verified against the live tracker, 2026-08-30

`bd dep tree <root> --direction=up --json` was run against this repo's own
tracker. Do not design the parser from `docs/design.md`'s field table alone —
it is close but not exact. What is actually there:

`created_at`, `created_by`, `depth`, `description`, `id`, `issue_type`,
`notes`, `owner`, `parent_id`, `priority`, `status`, `title`, `truncated`,
`updated_at`, plus `edge_from_parent`, `metadata`, `closed_at` and
`close_reason` **when non-empty**.

**Every optional field is omitempty — absent, not null.** Observed absent:
`edge_from_parent` on the root row, `metadata` on a bead with none,
`closed_at` and `close_reason` on anything not closed. `started_at` and
`assignee` were never observed at all; treat both as optional and do not
assume they exist.

This is the parse hazard for this task. "Fail loudly on an unexpected shape"
means a field of the **wrong type** is an error; a field that is simply
**missing** is normal and must deserialise to `None`.

**`metadata` is inline per row** — confirmed with a bead carrying
`agent_pane`. The design is right that badges need no second call.

## Known defect to fix as you reach it

**Unknown enum values are untested.** `Status::Other` and `Edge::Other` exist
so a new bd value does not break the parse, and nothing round-trips one. Feed
an unrecognised status and an unrecognised edge and assert they land in
`Other`. This is about compatibility with a future bd, not serde syntax.

## Definition of done

- `Bead` carries `issue_type` and, as options, `started_at` and `closed_at` —
  the JSON contract needs them and Task 8 cannot emit what is not parsed here.
- The fixture exercises **both shapes of every optional field**: a root row
  with no `edge_from_parent`, a child with one; a row with `metadata` and a row
  without; a closed row with `closed_at` and an open row without. A fixture
  where every row is the same shape produces a parser that breaks on the first
  real tracker.
- `truncated` is carried through, not ignored — a truncated node means the tree
  is incomplete, which is the silent partial answer this tool exists to avoid.
- A field of the wrong type is an error, not a default.
- Committed and pushed.

## Capturing fixtures

From *this machine's own* trackers only. `bdi-5yq` in this tracker carries an
`agent_pane` metadata key, set during prep precisely so a metadata-bearing row
can be captured; it is the closed smoke-test bead and exists to be poked.
notes:
bd's own depth is not trustworthy and Bead deliberately does not carry it. Measured on this tracker 2026-08-30: 'bd dep tree bdi-3um --direction=up --json --max-depth=2' does not mark deep nodes truncated — it reparents them. bdi-3um.4, .9 and .11 came back at depth 1 with parent_id rewritten to bdi-3um, losing their real parents. Task 4 already recomputes depth from the parent chain, which is the right call; the point is that parent_id is rewritten too, so a depth-limited call yields a different tree, not a marked-incomplete one.
Orchestrator, 2026-08-30: this note was recorded on this bead only, which is closed and which neither bdi-3um.4 nor bdi-3um.9 will read. Copied to both of those beads. A finding FOR another bead belongs ON that bead.
close_reason:
Pushed as 13110c9. model::types::{Bead,Status,Edge} and collect::bd::parse_dep_tree land with tests/fixtures/bd_dep_tree.json, a real six-row capture of bd dep tree --direction=up --json against this tracker. 13 tests in collect::bd, full suite 19 passing; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --check clean; nix build .#default produces a working bdi.

Two corrections to the bead's field notes, both from a fresh capture. (1) parent_id is present as an empty string on the root, not absent, matching docs/design.md:203 — parse_dep_tree normalises empty to None so Task 4 never files the root as dangling. (2) assignee and started_at are both present on every claimed bead; they are optional but not hypothetical.

Bead carries the design's whole field list (design.md:202-208): id, title, status, priority, issue_type, parent_id, edge_from_parent, metadata, owner, assignee, updated_at, started_at, closed_at, truncated. depth is deliberately not carried — see the note.

truncated is parsed and asserted, but no live bd row sets it: --max-depth flattens the tree instead of marking nodes truncated, so that assertion uses an inline literal.
